project_name: Texas Critical Data Centers Ector County campus
aliases: New Era / Sharon AI Ector County AI data center
Permian Basin Texas Critical Data Centers
developer: Texas Critical Data Centers LLC / New Era Energy & Digital / Sharon AI
status_detail: New Era describes Texas Critical Data Centers as its flagship Permian Basin, West Texas development with 1.4+ GW planned capacity on 492 acres and under development; county posted a June 10, 2026 data centers informational meeting hosted by Odessa Chamber economic development.
notes: Earlier 2025 reporting described an initial 250 MW AI/HPC phase in Ector County; company site now lists 1.4+ GW planned capacity and 492 acres for TCDC.

status_detail: No county-attributable data center project found in official county site/search results or broader web search; results were generic vendor SEO pages and unrelated Edwards Aquifer/data-center policy items.
notes: Visited Edwards County official site and searched data center/server farm terms; no project, permit, abatement, or EDA announcement located.

aliases: Northeast El Paso META Data Center
status_detail: City of El Paso data center page says the Meta/Wurldwide hyperscale AI campus was approved in December 2023, spans about 1,000 acres in Northeast El Paso, includes five construction phases, and phase 1 is underway; DCD reports Meta broke ground on a 1GW campus.
notes: Texas Comptroller lists Wurldwide LLC DBA Statue LLC as a registered qualifying large data center project effective 2025-09-17. KFOX says Meta later described the project as more than $10B with 300 permanent jobs.

aliases: Google Ellis County Midlothian data center
status_detail: Google's official Texas data center page says Texas is home to Google data center locations in Midlothian and Red Oak in Ellis County, and lists 2019 as the first Texas data center investment in Midlothian.
notes: Capacity not disclosed on Google's public location page.

project_name: Google Red Oak data center campus
status_detail: Google's official Texas page identifies Red Oak in Ellis County as a data center location and lists a 2023 milestone announcing another investment to build a second Texas data center in Red Oak.
notes: DCD reported initial $330M in 2023 and at least $600M over multiple years; local source said about 285,000 sq ft at 156 N. Austin Blvd.

status_detail: Compass announced its Red Oak campus after buying 225 acres and said it would deliver 350+ MW of IT load; Ellis County later announced a tax abatement partnership for Phase 2 construction of the Red Oak campus, stating Phase 2 would double production.
notes: Compass site indicates construction began in 2020; county's 2023 release documents Phase 2 tax abatement with City of Red Oak and Ellis County.

aliases: sixth data center campus in Red Oak
status_detail: CBS Texas reported Red Oak City Council approved a Compass Datacenters project in May 2026; the project would span roughly 830 acres and become the sixth data center campus in Red Oak.
notes: Kept separate from the earlier Compass Red Oak campus because reporting describes a newly approved 830-acre project/campus.

status_detail: DCD reports DataBank's Red Oak campus is planned on 292 acres for up to eight two-story facilities, 480 MW total, with phase one expected Q2 2026 and DFW9/DFW10 construction filings.
notes: TDLR-derived reporting places DFW9/DFW10 on Stainback Road in Red Oak, Ellis County; capacity from DCD campus reporting.

status_detail: No county-attributable project found after official Erath County site search and broader searches for data center/server farm/tax abatement terms.
notes: Search results were mostly generic social discussion, unrelated dispatch-center records, and Chapter 381 policy materials; no specific data center developer/site located.

project_name: Unidentified Falls County data center road-use agreement
status_detail: Falls County Commissioners Court minutes for 2025-12-22 include a commissioner asking for information on a data center road use agreement; no developer, site, or capacity found in official source. Separate Marlin Brushy Creek development reportedly withdrew but was not confirmed as a data center.
notes: Kept as unidentified to avoid losing the official road-use-agreement signal. The nearby Stargate/Burlington facility appears to be in Milam County, not Falls County, though Rosebud/Falls residents cite impacts.

status_detail: Fannin County local meeting coverage says commissioners discussed a Savoy Data Center on March 31, 2026; KXII reports Grayson County officials confirmed a data center is being built/planned in Fannin County on the Grayson County border, though land off Hwy 82 was not confirmed.
notes: Developer and exact parcel not found. Fannin County resolution supports responsible development but opposes high-potable-water/open-loop cooling safeguards gaps; citizen comments claimed high water use but those numbers are not independently verified.

status_detail: No specific Fayette County data center project found. Official county uploads include 2026 BESS/Data Center order and moratorium materials, indicating policy attention but not a named project/developer/site.
notes: Search results for Fayette County TX were dominated by county policy documents, generic vendor SEO, and unrelated Fayette County locations in other states.

status_detail: IREN's official Sweetwater page says the 2GW Sweetwater Hub spans two West Texas sites totaling 2,200 acres; Sweetwater 1 is under construction with 1,400 MW and Sweetwater 2 under construction with 600 MW. KTXS and DCD place the Sweetwater campus in Fisher County.
notes: Some third-party trackers split Sweetwater 2 into Nolan County; KTXS/DCD explicitly describe the Sweetwater campus/sites as in Fisher County, so included here under batch county.

project_name: Amazon Floyd County data center campus
status_detail: RFD News reports Floyd County commissioners are considering a Chapter 312 tax-abatement agreement for a proposed Amazon campus valued at more than $1B; the project could include seven data-center buildings across roughly 485 acres and would need air-cooled systems and self-supplied power under county negotiating terms.
notes: No county agenda packet/source with developer details found during quick pass; local news is explicit enough to include as planned.
